KS-2025-SB304.policyArea: Children and Minors, Health and Environment, Department of, Named Acts
KS-2025-SB304.aiSummary: The bill would require the state vital records office to send certain birth data to the state treasurer so the treasurer can mail information about savings accounts to families. It covers children born in Kansas, including those born before July 1, 2026 if they are still eligible, and children born on or after that date within 90 days of the birth record. The materials would explain a federal "Trump account," a 529 college savings plan, and an ABLE savings account for people with disabilities.

KS-2025-SB101.title: Creating the drug abuse resistance education (D.A.R.E.) educator position.

actions.text: Died in Committee
Referred to Senate Committee on Ways and Means
Introduced

KS-2025-SB101.aiSummary: The bill would have the attorney general appoint a statewide D.A.R.E. educator, with extra staff if money is available. The educator would teach drug abuse lessons in public elementary and secondary schools using an attorney general-approved curriculum that includes fentanyl and other opioid drugs. The educator would also report each year to lawmakers on curriculum changes and the schools served. If passed, the act would take effect after publication in the statute book.

KS-2025-HB2763.aiSummary: The bill would let Kansas join an interstate licensure compact for athletic trainers. It would let licensed athletic trainers in member states practice in other member states under set rules, while state licensing boards keep their role in licensing and discipline. It also sets shared rules for background checks, complaints, and sharing license and investigation info among member states.

KS-2025-HB2745.aiSummary: The bill would let voters approve some local property tax revenue increases for the next year, and it would set a ballot question for that vote. It would also create a property tax relief fund, with $60 million moved from the state general fund each year on July 15, rising by 2% starting in 2027, and send money to eligible counties for services like roads, law enforcement, elections, and public health and safety. Counties that hold the election would not get a payment from the fund. It would also keep the taxpayer notification costs fund in place for five more years.

It would expand Medicaid, called medical assistance here, for adults under 65 who are not pregnant and whose income is at or below 138% of the federal poverty level. KS-2025-HB2597.policyArea: Labor and Employment, Rules and Regulations, Administrative
KS-2025-HB2597.aiSummary: The bill would give Kansas employees paid sick leave. It would let workers earn at least 2 hours for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year, starting January 1, 2027, and it would set rules for when the leave could be used. The bill also says the state labor secretary would write rules to carry it out. It died in committee.

KS-2025-HB2065.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for picking Kansas delegates to a U.S. Constitution amendment convention called under Article V. It would say who appoints the delegates, how they can be recalled, and what limits they must follow when voting. It would also set pay for their travel and expenses and make it a felony to vote for an unauthorized amendment.

KS-2025-HB2051.aiSummary: The bill would require Kansas lawmakers to approve any national heritage area or national historic trail that goes beyond federal land in Kansas. It would also bar state money, including matching funds, from going to those designations unless lawmakers first approve it. State land, water, property, or facilities could not be included in such a designation without that approval.

KS-2025-HB2006.policyArea: Corrections, Department of, Retirement and Pensions
KS-2025-HB2006.aiSummary: The bill would move certain Department of Corrections security officers into the Kansas Police and Firemen's Retirement System, starting July 1, 2025. It would require employee and employer contributions for those members. It would also let eligible officers buy retirement credit for past security officer service under KPERS, either through ongoing payments or a lump sum.
